```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(csgjcr)
library(highcharter)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(reactable)

source("R/utils.R")
source("R/page-data.R")

# htmlwidgets seeds its element IDs from this, so rerenders give identical HTML
set.seed(2019)
```

```{r}
state_name_text <- "the United States"

srs_state_new <- read_srs_state()
latest_year <- max(srs_state_new$year)

### time series use an 11-year window ending in the latest data year
first_year <- latest_year - 10
srs_by_cat_us <- violent_totals(srs_state_new, first_year)
srs_us <- violent_by_offense(srs_state_new, first_year)

### US solve rates leave out the excluded states but apply to US reported counts
srs_by_cat_us_solve <- us_solve_trend(srs_state_new, first_year)
srs_us_solve <- us_solve_trend(srs_state_new, first_year, by_offense = TRUE)

### text and the state tables' U.S. total rows share these values
us_total <- total_rate_benchmark(srs_by_cat_us, base_year, latest_year, solves = srs_by_cat_us_solve)
solve_coverage <- read_solve_coverage()
us_solve_coverage <- solve_coverage$coverage[solve_coverage$state_name == "United States"]

### violent crime counts and rates by state, one column per year
### solve rates are multiplied by 100 for highcharts formatting
### excluded states get missing solve rates, so the maps gray them out
srs_state_to_map <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year %in% c(base_year, latest_year)) |>
  group_by(state_name, state_abbr, pop_total, year) |>
  summarize(
    n_reported = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_solved = sum(incidents_cleared, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    period = if_else(year == base_year, "base", "latest"),
    viol_crime_rate_100k = (n_reported / pop_total) * 100000,
    solved_rate = n_solved / n_reported * 100
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(state_name, state_abbr),
    names_from = period,
    values_from = c(n_reported, n_solved, viol_crime_rate_100k, solved_rate)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    solved_rate_percent_point_change = solved_rate_latest - solved_rate_base,
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change = (viol_crime_rate_100k_latest - viol_crime_rate_100k_base) / viol_crime_rate_100k_base * 100,
    across(starts_with("solved_rate_"), \(x) if_else(state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz, NA_real_, x))
  )

### map tooltips, one column per map, and links to each state's page
### changes show a sign, e.g., "+5%" or "-12%"
srs_state_to_map <- srs_state_to_map |>
  mutate(
    rate_label = format_rate_100k(viol_crime_rate_100k_latest),
    no_solve_data = paste0(
      state_name, " did not report enough data", "<br>",
      "on solved crime to the FBI to", "<br>",
      "make reliable estimates."
    ),
    tooltip_crime_change = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, "</b><br>",
      "Change in violent crime rate: ",
      sprintf("%+3d%%", as.numeric(comma(viol_crime_rate_percent_change, 1))), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k (", latest_year, "): ", format_rate_100k(viol_crime_rate_100k_latest), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k (", base_year, "): ", format_rate_100k(viol_crime_rate_100k_base)
    ),
    tooltip_crime_rate = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", latest_year, "</b><br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k: ", rate_label, "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(n_reported_latest, 1), "<br>"
    ),
    tooltip_solve_change = if_else(
      state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz, no_solve_data,
      paste0(
        "<b>", state_name, "</b><br>",
        "Change in solve rate: ",
        sprintf("%+3d", as.numeric(comma(solved_rate_percent_point_change, 1))), "<br>",
        "Solve rate (", latest_year, "): ", comma(solved_rate_latest, 1), "%", "<br>",
        "Solve rate (", base_year, "): ", comma(solved_rate_base, 1), "%", "<br>"
      )
    ),
    tooltip_solve_rate = if_else(
      state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz, no_solve_data,
      paste0(
        "<b>", state_name, " – ", latest_year, "</b><br>",
        "Solve rate: ", comma(solved_rate_latest, 1), "%", "<br>",
        "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(n_reported_latest, 1), "<br>",
        "Violent incidents solved: ", comma(n_solved_latest, 1)
      )
    ),
    url = paste0("https://projects.csgjusticecenter.org/tools-for-states-to-address-crime/50-state-crime-data/?state=", tolower(state_abbr)),
    no_solve_data = NULL
  )

### describe a set of states for text, e.g., "12 states and the District of Columbia"
describe_states <- function(abbr) {
  n <- sum(abbr != "DC")
  paste0(n, if_else(n == 1, " state", " states"), if_else("DC" %in% abbr, " and the District of Columbia", ""))
}

states_rate_down <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(viol_crime_rate_percent_change < 0) |> pull(state_abbr)
states_rate_up <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(viol_crime_rate_percent_change > 0) |> pull(state_abbr)

states_solved_down <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(solved_rate_percent_point_change < 0) |> pull(state_abbr)
states_solved_up <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(solved_rate_percent_point_change > 0) |> pull(state_abbr)

### national violent crime rate change and offenses lower or higher than the base year
us_rate_change <- us_total$rate_change / 100

offense_rate_change <- srs_us |>
  filter(year %in% c(base_year, latest_year)) |>
  summarize(change = incidents_reported_rate_total[year == latest_year] - incidents_reported_rate_total[year == base_year], .by = group)

offenses_lower <- offense_rate_change |> filter(change < 0) |> pull(group) |> tolower()
offenses_higher <- offense_rate_change |> filter(change > 0) |> pull(group) |> tolower()

### import and prep hex map geo
hex <- sf::read_sf("data/us_states_hexgrid.geojson") |>
  select(state_abb = iso3166_2)

hex_gj <- hex |>
  sf::st_transform(3857) |>
  geojsonsf::sf_geojson() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

```{r }
### national police protection expenditures in dollars of the latest survey year
asslgf_clean_national <- read_police_spending("US", read_inflation_index())

### national violent crime counts for officer workload
violent_us_by_year <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent") |>
  summarize(n_violent_reported = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE), .by = year)

  left_join(violent_us_by_year, by = "year") |>
```

# Trends in violent crime and accountability

## Violent crime is down, but unsolved crime keeps piling up.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r }
# ==============================================================================
# Crime Without Consequence, page 1: two accessible highcharter charts
#   Chart 1 (hc_reported_solved): Violent crime reported, solved, and unsolved
#            in the U.S., 2020-2025
#   Chart 2 (hc_backlog): Backlog of unsolved violent crime, 2020-2025
# ==============================================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PREP DATA FOR FIRST SECTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crime_data <- srs_by_cat_us_solve |>
  ### filter on years in handout
  filter(year%in%c(2020:2025)) |> 
  mutate(
    cumulative_incidents_unsolved = cumsum(incidents_unsolved)     # backlog added since 2020
  )

# hc_setup() shows each point's `tooltip` column, so build that text per chart.
# Chart 1: one tooltip per year listing all three values.
trend_data <- crime_data |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0(
    "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
    "Violent crimes reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
    "Violent crimes solved: ", comma(incidents_solved, 1), "<br>",
    "Violent crimes unsolved: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1)
  ))

# Chart 2: backlog tooltip.
backlog_data <- crime_data |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0(
    "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
    "Unsolved crimes added since 2020: ", comma(cumulative_incidents_unsolved, 1), "<br>",
    "Unsolved this year: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1)
  ))

```

```{r }
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COLORS (from the handout) AND SMALL HELPERS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
col_navy <- "#001E35"   # reported line, backlog fill
col_blue <- "#005DA6"   # solved line, callout outline
col_gap  <- "#CCE9FF"   # shaded "unsolved" gap
col_teal <- "#2DEBC3"   # accent markers

# Axis labels: 0, 500K, 1M, 1.5M
crime_js_axis_label <- JS("function() {
  var v = this.value;
  if (v === 0) return '0';
  return v >= 1e6 ? (v / 1e6) + 'M' : (v / 1e3) + 'K';
}")

# Axis labels with a leading plus: +1M, +2M ... The baseline shows a blue "?"
# (as in the handout) because the pre-2020 backlog is unknown.
crime_js_axis_label_plus <- JS("function() {
  var v = this.value;
  if (v === 0) return '<span style=\"color:#005DA6;font-weight:900\">?</span>';
  return '+' + (v / 1e6) + 'M';
}")

# "Not starting at zero" note with an angled dotted line (render event).
# Draws a blue dotted line from the note down-left to the axis near the
# baseline "?", matching the handout. It is redrawn on every render (resize,
# print), so the previous copy is destroyed first. Positions come from the
# plot area, so it scales with the chart; tweak the 0.4 (start height),
# 0.05 (end height above baseline) and 170 (note width) to taste.
crime_js_note_line <- JS("function() {
  var chart = this, accent = '#005DA6';
  if (chart.noteGroup) chart.noteGroup.destroy();
  var g = chart.renderer.g('not-starting-at-zero-note').attr({ zIndex: 7 }).add();
  chart.noteGroup = g;
  var plotH = chart.plotHeight;
  var xEnd = chart.plotLeft + 2;                         // at the y-axis
  var yEnd = chart.plotTop + plotH - 0.05 * plotH;       // just above baseline
  var xTop = xEnd + 16;                                  // angled up and right
  var yTop = chart.plotTop + 0.4 * plotH;
  chart.renderer.path(['M', xTop, yTop, 'L', xEnd, yEnd])
    .attr({ stroke: accent, 'stroke-width': 1.5, 'stroke-dasharray': '3,3', fill: 'none' })
    .add(g);
  // SVG text (not an HTML label) so the tooltip draws on top of the note.
  // Highcharts wraps SVG text at the css width.
  var html = '<span style=\"color:' + accent + ';font-weight:700\">Not starting at zero:</span> ' +
             'added on top of unsolved crimes from before 2020';
  var note = chart.renderer.text(html, 0, 0)
    .css({ width: Math.min(170, chart.plotWidth * 0.5) + 'px',
           color: '#000000', fontSize: '13px' })
    .attr({ zIndex: 7 })
    .add(g);
  var box = note.getBBox();                 // measured at y = 0
  note.attr({ x: xTop - 4, y: yTop - 6 - (box.y + box.height) });  // sit just above the line
}")

# Tooltip position for chart 2: beside the point (right of it, flipping left
# near the plot's right edge) and centered on it vertically, kept inside the
# plot. This keeps tooltips clear of the "not starting at zero" note at the
# top-left, and off the point itself.
crime_js_tooltip_position <- JS("function(labelWidth, labelHeight, point) {
  var chart = this.chart, gap = 12;
  var px = chart.plotLeft + point.plotX, py = chart.plotTop + point.plotY;
  var x = px + gap;
  if (x + labelWidth > chart.plotLeft + chart.plotWidth) x = px - labelWidth - gap;
  var y = Math.min(Math.max(py - labelHeight / 2, chart.plotTop),
                   chart.plotTop + chart.plotHeight - labelHeight);
  return { x: x, y: y };
}")

# Point labels: 1.31M, 563K
crime_js_point_label <- JS("function() {
  var v = this.y;
  return v >= 1e6 ? (v / 1e6).toFixed(2) + 'M' : Math.round(v / 1e3) + 'K';
}")

# Direct line label: the series name on the LAST point only
crime_js_end_label <- JS("function() {
  return this.point.index === this.series.data.length - 1 ? this.series.name : null;
}")

# Long text description for screen readers. It sets only `description`, so the
# accessibility options hc_setup() already set are kept.
crime_hc_describe <- function(chart, text) {
  chart$x$hc_opts$accessibility$description <- text
  chart
}

# Source line shared by both charts
crime_caption <- "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances"
```

## 2020–2025 change 

```{r }
#| fig-height: 5.5

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CHART 1: Reported, solved, and unsolved
#
# The shaded "unsolved" gap is two stacked area series: an invisible base that
# follows the solved line, with the unsolved amount stacked on top in light
# blue. (This avoids the arearange type, which needs an extra module.)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
desc_trend <- paste0(
  "Line chart with a shaded gap, 2020 to 2025. Violent crimes reported fell from ",
  comma(first(crime_data$incidents_reported), 1), " in 2020 to ",
  comma(last(crime_data$incidents_reported), 1), " in 2025. Violent crimes solved stayed between ",
  comma(min(crime_data$incidents_solved), 1), " and ", comma(max(crime_data$incidents_solved), 1),
  " each year. The shaded area between the two lines is the number left unsolved each year: ",
  comma(first(crime_data$incidents_unsolved), 1), " in 2020 and ",
  comma(last(crime_data$incidents_unsolved), 1), " in 2025."
)

# Height of the label point for "Unsolved": halfway between the two lines in 2022
gap_label_data <- crime_data |>
  filter(year == 2022) |>
  transmute(year, mid = (incidents_reported + incidents_solved) / 2)

hc_reported_solved <- hchart(
  # Series 1: invisible base of the stack (follows the solved line)
  trend_data, "area", hcaes(year, incidents_solved),
  name = "Solved (base of gap)", color = "transparent", fillOpacity = 0,
  lineWidth = 0, stacking = "normal", marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
  enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 0,
  accessibility = list(enabled = FALSE)
) |>

  # Series 2: the shaded gap = unsolved, stacked on the base
  hc_add_series(
    trend_data, "area", hcaes(year, incidents_unsolved),
    name = "Unsolved", color = col_gap, fillOpacity = 1, lineWidth = 0,
    stacking = "normal", marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
    enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 0,
    accessibility = list(
      description = "Shaded area showing violent crimes left unsolved each year.",
      point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
        "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes unsolved: {point.y:,.0f}")
    )
  ) |>

  # Series 3: invisible helper that carries the "Unsolved" label inside the gap
  hc_add_series(
    gap_label_data, "line", hcaes(year, mid),
    name = "Unsolved (label)", lineWidth = 0, marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
    enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 1,
    dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "Unsolved", align = "center",
                      verticalAlign = "middle", y = 0, allowOverlap = TRUE,
                      style = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "15px",
                                   fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none")),
    accessibility = list(enabled = FALSE)
  ) |>

  # Series 4: reported (solid navy line). Value labels above each point, plus a
  # direct "Reported" label at the end of the line in place of a legend.
  hc_add_series(
    trend_data, "line", hcaes(year, incidents_reported),
    name = "Reported", color = col_navy, lineWidth = 3, zIndex = 2,
    marker = list(symbol = "circle", radius = 4, lineColor = "#FFFFFF", lineWidth = 1.5),
    dataLabels = list(
      list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_point_label,
           verticalAlign = "bottom", y = -6,
           style = list(color = col_navy, fontSize = "13px",
                        fontWeight = "400", textOutline = "none")),
      list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_end_label,
           align = "left", verticalAlign = "middle", x = 10, y = 0,
           crop = FALSE, overflow = "allow", allowOverlap = TRUE,
           style = list(color = col_navy, fontSize = "15px",
                        fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none"))
    ),
    accessibility = list(
      description = "Violent crimes reported each year.",
      point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
        "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes reported: {point.y:,.0f}")
    )
  ) |>

  # Series 5: solved (dashed blue line, diamond markers). Dash style and marker
  # shape separate it from the reported line without relying on color alone.
  hc_add_series(
    trend_data, "line", hcaes(year, incidents_solved),
    name = "Solved", color = col_blue, lineWidth = 3, dashStyle = "ShortDash",
    zIndex = 2,
    marker = list(symbol = "diamond", radius = 5, lineColor = "#FFFFFF", lineWidth = 1.5),
    dataLabels = list(
      list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_point_label,
           verticalAlign = "top", y = 8,
           style = list(color = col_blue, fontSize = "13px",
                        fontWeight = "400", textOutline = "none")),
      list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_end_label,
           align = "left", verticalAlign = "middle", x = 10, y = 0,
           crop = FALSE, overflow = "allow", allowOverlap = TRUE,
           style = list(color = col_blue, fontSize = "15px",
                        fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none"))
    ),
    accessibility = list(
      description = "Violent crimes solved each year.",
      point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
        "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes solved: {point.y:,.0f}")
    )
  ) |>

  hc_title(text = "Violent Crime Reported, Solved, and Unsolved in the U.S., 2020–2025") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Violent crimes reported to police per year") |>
  hc_caption(text = crime_caption) |>
  # No legend: lines are labeled at their ends and the gap inside the chart
  hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>

  # Site defaults: theme, exporting, accessibility module, tooltip, no animation
  hc_setup() |>

  # Chart-specific settings go AFTER hc_setup() so they merge into its defaults.
  # Explicit ticks keep whole years despite the padding that makes room for
  # the end labels; reversedStacks = FALSE puts the base series at the bottom.
  hc_xAxis(tickPositions = 2020:2025, min = 2019.6, max = 2025.4) |>
  hc_yAxis(min = 0, max = 1500000, tickInterval = 500000, reversedStacks = FALSE,
           labels = list(formatter = crime_js_axis_label)) |>
  hc_chart(marginRight = 70) |>
  crime_hc_describe(desc_trend)


hc_reported_solved

```

## 2020–2025 backlog 

```{r }
#| fig-height: 5.5

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CHART 2: Backlog of unsolved violent crime (cumulative area)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
desc_backlog <- paste0(
  "Filled area chart, 2020 to 2025. The backlog of unsolved violent crimes added ",
  "since 2020 grows every year, from ", comma(first(crime_data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved), 1),
  " at the end of 2020 to ", comma(last(crime_data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved), 1),
  " by the end of 2025. The chart does not start from zero in real terms: these crimes ",
  "are added on top of an unknown number of unsolved crimes from before 2020."
)

hc_backlog <- hchart(
  backlog_data, "area", hcaes(year, cumulative_incidents_unsolved),
  name = "Backlog added since 2020",
  color = col_navy, fillOpacity = 1, lineWidth = 2,
  marker = list(enabled = TRUE, symbol = "circle", radius = 4,
                fillColor = col_teal, lineColor = col_navy, lineWidth = 1.5),
  # Label only the last point (e.g. +4.3M)
  dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, align = "right", verticalAlign = "bottom", y = -8,
                    formatter = JS("function() {
                      return this.point.index === this.series.data.length - 1
                        ? '+' + (this.y / 1e6).toFixed(1) + 'M' : null;
                    }"),
                    style = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "13px",
                                 fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none")),
  accessibility = list(
    description = "Cumulative unsolved violent crimes added to the backlog since 2020.",
    point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
      "year: {point.x:.0f}, unsolved violent crimes added since 2020: {point.y:,.0f}")
  )
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Backlog of Unsolved Violent Crime, 2020–2025") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Unsolved violent crimes added since 2020") |>
  hc_caption(text = crime_caption) |>
  hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
  hc_setup() |>
  hc_xAxis(tickPositions = 2020:2025, min = 2019.7, max = 2025.3) |>
  hc_yAxis(min = 0, max = 5000000, tickInterval = 1000000,
           labels = list(formatter = crime_js_axis_label_plus, useHTML = TRUE)) |>
  # Same way the site attaches end_labels: add the render event after hc_setup()
  hc_chart(events = list(render = crime_js_note_line)) |>
  # Keep tooltips from covering the note (set after hc_setup(), which supplies
  # the tooltip text formatter; this only changes where the box appears)
  hc_tooltip(positioner = crime_js_tooltip_position) |>
  crime_hc_describe(desc_backlog)

hc_backlog
```

```{r}
state_map_specs <- list(
  crime_change = list(
    value = "viol_crime_rate_percent_change", tooltip = "tooltip_crime_change",
    title = paste0("Change in violent crime, ", base_year, "–", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Percent change in crime reported to police per 100,000 residents",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates",
    colors = change_colors, label_format = "{value}%", legend_width = 250,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, percent change: {point.value:.1f}",
    symmetric = TRUE
  ),
  crime_rate = list(
    value = "viol_crime_rate_100k_latest", tooltip = "tooltip_crime_rate",
    title = paste0("Violent crime rate, ", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Crime reported to police per 100,000 residents",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates",
    colors = rate_colors, label_format = "{value:,.0f}", legend_width = 250,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, violent crime rate: {point.rate_label}"
  ),
  solve_change = list(
    value = "solved_rate_percent_point_change", tooltip = "tooltip_solve_change",
    title = paste0("Change in percentage of violent crime solved, ", base_year, "–", latest_year),
    subtitle = paste0("Percentage point change in rate of solved violent crimes from ", base_year, " to ", latest_year),
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances",
    colors = rev(change_colors), label_format = "{value}", legend_width = 300,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, percentage point change: {point.value:.1f}",
    symmetric = TRUE, null_interaction = TRUE
  ),
  solve_rate = list(
    value = "solved_rate_latest", tooltip = "tooltip_solve_rate",
    title = paste0("Solved violent crime, ", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Percentage of violent crimes solved",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances",
    colors = rate_colors, label_format = "{value}%", legend_width = 400,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, solve rate: {point.value:.1f}%",
    null_interaction = TRUE
  )
)

state_map_chart(srs_state_to_map, hex_gj, state_map_specs$crime_change)
```

The national violent crime rate was `r percent(abs(us_rate_change), 1, suffix = " percent")` `r if_else(us_rate_change < 0, "lower", "higher")` in `r latest_year` than in `r base_year`. In `r latest_year`, rates of `r knitr::combine_words(offenses_lower)` were lower than in `r base_year``r if (length(offenses_higher) > 0) paste0(", while the rate of ", knitr::combine_words(offenses_higher), " was higher")`.

Trends in violent crime also varied by state. Between `r base_year` and `r latest_year`, violent crime rates decreased in `r describe_states(states_rate_down)` and increased in `r describe_states(states_rate_up)`.

## Trends in solved violent crime

In `r latest_year`, `r solve_rate_text(us_total$solve_rate)` of violent crime incidents reported to police in the United States were solved. The percentage of violent crimes that law enforcement solved fell from 2019 to 2021 and rose each year from 2022 to `r max(srs_by_cat_us_solve$year)`, reaching its highest level since at least `r min(srs_by_cat_us_solve$year)`.

Data regarding crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr). Violent crime includes homicide, aggravated assault, robbery, and rape. Crime rates are calculated by dividing the number of estimated incidents by the total population for a given geography. Solve rates are the number of reported crimes cleared by arrest or by exceptional means divided by the number of reported crimes. For more information, see the [data sources and methodology](#methodology) section below.

## Data sources and methodology

Data on crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr){target="_parent"}. Counts of reported violent crime from `r min(srs_by_cat_us$year)` through `r latest_year` come from the Summary Reporting System (SRS) and the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS). The FBI estimates reported crime for each state from agency-level reports, accounting for agencies that did not report, and publishes these estimates on its [Crime Data Explorer](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}.

State solve rates are calculated by dividing crimes cleared by crimes reported among agencies that reported to the FBI. Solved crimes are estimated by multiplying each state's solve rate by the FBI's estimate of its reported crimes. The U.S. solve rate divides the total of these estimated solved crimes across states by the total of estimated reported crimes. Each offense has its own solve rate, so solved counts by offense may not add up to the violent crime total.

The FBI stopped collecting SRS data after 2020 and required agencies to report through NIBRS. Fewer agencies reported as a result, so `r low_coverage_solve_year` estimates are less reliable. Agencies covering `r percent(us_solve_coverage, 1, suffix = " percent")` of the U.S. population reported in `r low_coverage_solve_year`. State pages show `r low_coverage_solve_year` solve rates only where reporting agencies covered at least `r percent(min_solve_coverage, suffix = " percent")` of the state's population. Starting with 2022 data, the FBI again accepted SRS reports from agencies that could not submit NIBRS data. In 2025, agencies reporting through NIBRS or SRS covered 96.2 percent of the U.S. population, and agencies reporting through NIBRS covered 89.5 percent, according to the FBI's [*Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2025*](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/resources/reports/UCR_Summary_of_Reported_Crimes_in_the_Nation_2025.pdf){target="_parent"}.`r low_coverage_text`

Crime rates are calculated by dividing estimated reported crimes by the total population. Population data come from the U.S. Census Bureau [Population Estimates Program](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html){target="_parent"}.

Crime counts follow the FBI's hierarchy rule, which counts only the most serious offense in each incident. Homicide ranks highest, followed by rape, robbery, and aggravated assault. An incident that includes both a robbery and an aggravated assault, for example, counts as one robbery.

{{< include _methodology-exceptional-clearance.qmd >}}

U.S. solve rates leave out `r knitr::combine_words(states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz)`, which did not report reliable clearance data. In 2022, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) reported crimes to the FBI but no clearances. For that year, New York's solve rates for all violent crime, aggravated assault, and robbery use the average of the NYPD's four [quarterly clearance reports](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/stats/reports-analysis/clearance.page){target="_parent"}. In 2019 and 2020, those reports matched the NYPD's FBI clearance rates within half a percentage point for aggravated assault and robbery but not for homicide and rape. New York's 2022 homicide and rape solve rates are therefore omitted, and New York is left out of the 2022 U.S. homicide and rape solve rates.

Data on law enforcement expenditures come from the U.S. Census Bureau [Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances.html){target="_parent"}. Expenditures include police protection spending by state governments and all local governments in each state, such as counties and municipalities. Expenditures are in dollars of the most recent year, adjusted with the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (C-CPI-U), following the [Census Bureau's guidance](https://www.census.gov/topics/income-poverty/income/guidance/current-vs-constant-dollars.html){target="_parent"}.

Officer counts include sworn officers in state and local law enforcement agencies as of October 31 of each year, from the FBI's [Crime Data Explorer law enforcement employee data](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Officers per capita uses the population served by agencies that reported employee counts. Officers per violent crime divides that rate by the national violent crime rate from the FBI's state estimates.

{{< include _methodology-shr.qmd >}}

:::
